t20: Dice board games are based on a simple cycle: roll the dice, move forward, do what the square tells you. Roll or Dare adds 1000+ tasks, a point system, monsters, mini games and a Fate Wheel to this cycle. Learning the rules takes two minutes; by the end of the first round nobody asks about rules.
t21: This guide has been updated for the new Roll or Dare version released in September 2026 (Adventure Island, monsters, mini games, team mode).
t23: When the game opens, you get match settings first. Four choices are made here, everything else is automatic:
t27: City (simple, fast) or Adventure Island (52 squares, special squares, monsters).
t29: Family (all ages), Party (friend gatherings) and Bold (18+). Turn on whatever you want.
t31: Each player rolls the dice this many times. Default is 3; reduce for large groups, increase for small ones.
t32: Then players are added: 2–10 people, names, and a piece chosen from 12 characters (cat, penguin, ninja, yeti, cactus…). In team mode, players are split into two teams.

t51: On normal squares, the task gives points equal to the square's value: low-point squares bring warm-up tasks everyone can do easily, high-point squares take a little courage. Adventure Island adds special squares:

t89: Monsters only appear in monster lairs, but can also rarely pop up on regular task squares. If it disrupts the pace, turn off Monsters in match settings.
t91: The game works on one phone with 2 to 10 players. With two players, the pace is fast but task variety drops; the most efficient range is 4–7 players. For groups of ten, the turn length stretches, so reducing round count or switching to
t93: gives better results: points accumulate for teams, and everyone stays in the game even while waiting their turn.
t95: Each completed task gives points equal to the square's value; double on gold squares, +30 to the winner in duels, bonuses for streaks. When the match setting's round count is up, the game ends and the podium appears: first, second, third; confetti, fun end-game rewards, and rematch with one tap. Player stats accumulate across matches.

t97: Small tweaks that make the game better
t98: Set the round count by group size: fewer for large groups, more for small ones.
t99: Play the first game on City board; when the group grasps the cycle, switch to Adventure Island.
t100: In family settings, keep only Family category on; Party and Bold (18+) have adult tasks.

t106: How many people play Roll or Dare?
t107: 2 to 10 players on one phone. The smoothest experience is 4–7 players; large groups can be split into Red and Blue with team mode.
t108: What happens if a task isn't done?
t109: When I Couldn't is pressed, that square's points aren't taken and the turn passes to the next player; no extra penalty. A player who doesn't like a task can use their joker to change it.
t111: It ends when the round count set in match settings is up; each player rolls the dice that many times. The player or team with the highest score reaches the top of the podium.
t112: Does Roll or Dare need internet?
t113: The game plays locally on one phone, but since it's free and shows ads after matches, you need an active internet connection.
t115: Yes. In match settings, keep only Family category on; Party and Bold (18+) categories have adult tasks.
